A reference check is the moment when your customer sells for you, and you are not in the room. So prepare your customer, but never write their answers. Before the call, I tell the customer three things: who the buyer is, what the buyer is worried about, and that a candid answer is better than a perfect one. Buyers do not trust a reference with no drawback. If your customer says there was a hiccup and the supplier fixed it fast, that is worth more than any testimonial on your website. After the call, I always ask the customer two questions: what did the buyer ask, and what did you say? Then I write it down for the sales team on the same day.

Hi Flavio, it's Davide. I just finished the call with Paola Ferri. She asked a lot of questions, and they were all fair. She asked if the connector was ready on time, and I told her the truth: it was two weeks late. She also asked about the reports, and I said they were our main drawback. But she was very interested when I told her about our approval time. At the end, she asked if she could visit one of our warehouses in person, and I said yes. So expect a call from Giulia. And one more thing, Flavio. Paola said she would be ready to make a decision in two weeks. Good luck.
